content.text:
The drawing is a tricyclic fused aromatic system with two N atoms at the bottom, each adjacent to the central ring fusion carbons. That is 1,10-phenanthroline.

Reading the rings:
- The left ring has N at the bottom right, bonded to a fusion carbon at about (700, 780) and to a CH at (550, 868).
- The central ring has the top CH=CH at (700, 607) and (800, 607), and the two fusion carbons at the bottom (700, 780) and (800, 780).
- The right ring is the mirror image of the left, with N at the bottom left.

SMILES for 1,10-phenanthroline: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1cccnc12

Check of the ring connectivity:
- Atoms are c1 (C3), c (C2), n (N1), c2 (C10b), c(c1) (C4a, closing the left ring through C4), then cc (C5, C6), c1 (C6a), ccc (C7, C8, C9), n (N10), and c12 (C10a).
- The left ring is c1, c, n, c2, c(c1), which gives 6 atoms: C3, C2, N1, C10b, C4a and C4. The atom "c1" inside the parentheses is C4, which closes to C3. That is correct.
- The central ring is C10b, C4a, C5, C6, C6a, C10a, which is 6 atoms.
- The right ring is C6a, C7, C8, C9, N10, C10a, which is 6 atoms.

SMILES: c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1cccnc12
